chunks.l2: The supreme Lord, here, is made of light — and light is made of awareness. An objector asks: granted He is light by nature, why should He not be bare knowing, the way the calm-brahman teachers have it? The answer specifies awareness two ways — bounded and boundless — so that the bounded knower of the void does not put a ceiling on consciousness-light. In creating, awareness wears the world's shape; in sustaining, it shines the world forth; in withdrawing, it takes all back into itself — everywhere the thrill of a full and complete I. Awareness, in short, is the flash of an I that was never put together — through world-shaping, world-lighting, world-dissolving. And if that awareness were missing, lordlessness and deadness would follow — as sunlight, which lacks awareness, leans on something else to shine and sinks to the side of the inert.
chunks.l3:
The supreme Lord is light through and through — and light, rightly seen, is awareness through and through.
"But why not bare knowing," comes the objection, "the calm brahman praised by the school of stillness?"
Because awareness is twofold — bound and boundless — lest the bounded knower, even of the void, set a ceiling on the light.
In creating it takes the world's shape; in keeping, it lights the world; in withdrawing, it gathers all back into itself — everywhere the delight of a whole and perfect I.
Awareness is simply this: the flash of an I nobody made — through shaping, shining, dissolving.
Take it away, and lordship goes with it, and deadness: sunlight, which knows nothing, must borrow its shining from another and sinks to the side of the inert.

chunks.l2: This very awareness is what the scriptures trumpet under many names: consciousness, consciousness-in-its-freedom, the supreme Word risen from its own sap, freedom, the supreme Self's sovereign majesty, doership, pulsing, essence, heart, vibration — and more. In the Śaiva teaching, the scriptures everywhere proclaim one thing: that awareness comes first in the light of consciousness, sung in scripture after scripture in different words. Consciousness — because awareness is the Self's own chief form. The supreme Word — because it speaks the world into declaration by grasping it back, supreme as the ground and fullness of all lesser graspings, risen from its own sap because its "I" never sets, full-bodied consciousness. Freedom — because it binds the cast-out "this" back to the self, looses it again, and lays it low through the stations of the void — differing from the inert by exactly these marks. Sovereignty — needing nothing else when the world begins, unlike Brahmā and his fellow wardens of māyā's womb, who answer to another's will and bend to fate. Doership — raising the whole world, from Śiva down to earth, into "this"-ness out of inward shining oneness, the way a yogin makes things — an unsurpassed kind of causing. Pulsing — the relation of flashing, and it is mine: were throbbing nobody's in particular, everything would flash for everyone always, and all would be omniscient, or all blind. Essence — the untrifling form, the Lord's own power of awareness. Heart — where the world comes to rest. Vibration — the still light of consciousness shimmering with motion, the world appearing as something extra where nothing extra is.

chunks.l2: And therefore — the unmade I, real, self-lit in form — the supreme Lord pulses and shines by the power of the supreme Lady, taking the shape of the world from Śiva down to clay. This very shining is His making of the world — and the world's being alive. But what kind of "made" is the world — made as something different from Him, or as nothing different? If different, His freedom breaks; if not different, how is it made at all? The answer: without another's light the world cannot even be noticed, let alone come into its own — its coming to wear a shining body, leaning on His ground, is exactly what "made" means here. Māyā's own freedom puts difference on display, so the world is handled as different while being nothing different. "Made," in the end, means nothing but shining-by-Him. Formed this way, the world is nothing apart from Maheśvara the maker, who is shining-formed. For if what is known stood apart, it could not shine, and no shining could reach it — there would be nothing at all, and all the traffic of taking and giving would collapse. And if the world is nothing apart from the Lord, must He not be stained by resemblance to a merely shining world — veiled by it? Rather the would-be veil destroys itself: gained even within the self, veiling the light would unmake itself. By this world, then, the Lord's light-formed nature is never veiled — the world, given rest by His shining, has become His very life-breath. How could it throttle Him — and throttling Him, itself go on standing?
chunks.l3:
So the unmade I — real, lit by itself — the Lord pulses and shines by his Lady's power in the shape of the world from Śiva to clay.
This shining is his making, and the world's being alive.
"But made how — as something other than him, or as nothing other?" As other, his freedom breaks; as nothing other, what is there to make?
The answer: without another's light the world cannot so much as be noticed, let alone come into its own — its coming to bear a shining body, leaning on his ground, is exactly what "made" means.
Difference is put on display by freedom's own magic, so the world is handled as different while being nothing different: to be made is to shine by him, and nothing else.
Formed this way the world is nothing apart from Maheśvara the maker.
For stood the known apart, it could not shine and no shining could reach it — there would be nothing at all, and all the give and take of the world would fall.
"Then must he not be stained by likeness, veiled by a shining world?" Rather the would-be veil unmakes itself: caught even inside the self, in veiling light it vanishes.
By this world his light-shape is never veiled — the world, given rest by his shining, has grown into his very breath.
How should it choke him — and choking him, itself go on standing?

chunks.l2: Indicators and causes cannot get a grip on the Lord, proved before all proof — and since even the knower who lays down injunctions exists in His likeness, that knower's standing proved does not hang on any proof. His self-lit-ness is proved by experience. "What proves that He is?" — grant that things are. "What proves one of such a nature?" — the proof is the questioner's own shape: the self-shining of Maheśvara, proved before all, is proved for everyone by feeling oneself. Consciousness-light itself, the life of everything, appoints proofs for the business of illusion — but for Him no proof is ever used, since everything else, being inert, cannot light even itself without another's light, let alone settle anything beyond itself. Proof itself is proof only by leaning on Him — and for the proving of Him, who is proof's own life, what use is poor proof, whose office is to let some fresh flash come to rest, marked as a finding, inside the knower? The knower, ever-lit, his shining unbroken, already enjoys every finding tucked inward within himself — where would a fresh flash be put to use in him, and where else could its finding come to rest? So proof is for knowables like body and breath, blue and pleasure — not for the Lord, who is proof's life. Hence the saying: the proofs that draw out the very life of things — beyond them all stands a further Life, and He is the supreme Lord.

chunks.l2: Now what each is like. The Śiva-level is supreme Śiva Himself — will, knowing, and doing in one form, pure and full bliss by nature — throbbing within every knower as full-I joy, beyond every level, vast-bodied light that can hold a hundred thousand reflections of world-makings and world-unmakings. When the Lord takes on the will to send the world forth, His first pulse is already will-power's level — out of His own freedom's greatness, wishing to bloom outward, brimming with supreme-bliss joy, the grasp "I": power's level. The world, just now sprouting, stands covered over with I-by-the-self — the eternal-Śiva level: with the this-portion bloomed faintly upon the ground of pure consciousness only, will comes first. The sprouted world, standing wrapped in I — the Lord level: the I sprinkled over a clarified this, knowing comes first, the two differing only in how dim or undim the this-portion is. The grasp of I-and-this as one is pure knowledge: when, amid full-grown difference flashing, the I shines up as nothing but consciousness, the scales-held-even "I-this" grasp — doing comes first: knowledge's level. Spreading difference among things already of His own nature is illusion: achieving the hardest of feats, growing the pride of knowerhood in the unconscious and the void, making even one-with-consciousness things appear divided, hiding their own form — and the stuff all things from art to clay are made of. But when the Lord, by the Lady's power of illusion — which is only another name for freedom — veils His own form and puts on the tight mask of knowerhood, He is called the person — Himself, deluded by illusion, bound by deeds, taking his deeds for his chains — the wanderer, wandering. Time is what cuts the sequence of things as they shine and unshine — "I knew, I know, I will know; I did, I do, I will do" — measuring even things in the shape of knowing and doing, it cuts them off: past and the rest. Necessity is what holds him to "this is mine to do, that is not mine to do" — manifold shapes of must, fixed fruit from fixed cause among them. These five, by veiling His own form, are called the sheath — other than His form, yet not other, lying over the nature of full consciousness like a cover. The root-cause of the levels from the great down to earth is nature — goodness, passion, and darkness in equipoise: pleasure, pain, and delusion by make, shining, doing, and holding by nature — an undivided poise where part and counterpoint cannot be told apart. What decides — "this is such" — holding the mirror up to passing thoughts, fit by clarity to catch reflections, is intellect. What means "mine, not mine" in pride is ego. What means resolve is mind. These three are the inner organ — grasping inner things like pleasure, made of the strands in part-and-counterpoint, and the cause of the sense-and-gross heap to come. The means of grasping sounds, touches, forms, tastes, smells in order are ear, skin, eye, tongue, nose — the five knowing senses. The means of speaking, taking, moving, voiding, and blissful action in order are voice, hands, feet, evacuation, generation — the five doing senses. Sounds, touches, forms, tastes, smells in their common shape — that and nothing more, with no inner distinctions — are the five subtles. Ether gives room; air keeps alive; fire burns and cooks; water refreshes and flows; earth upholds.

chunks.l2: As sprout and leaf and fruit stand in the banyan seed in bodies exactly fitted to them, so this whole world in all its varied makings stands inside the seed of the heart — as in peacock-egg juice the craftsman's skill already holds every feather's line and plume-variety, for those rich in attention to weigh with subtle sight. "As the great tree stands in the banyan seed in power-form, so this world, moving and unmoving, stands in the heart-seed": by this traditional maxim, in the heart-seed shaped as the supreme Lady this world is contained. How so? As the ultimate truth of pot and bowl, clay's transformations, is clay itself — as watery kinds, examined, settle into water-in-common — so the levels from earth to illusion, examined for what is real in them, prove to be being itself. Even of the word "being" itself: strip the suffix that shows the root's sense, and the bare-stem letter s alone is left — and inside it stand thirty-one levels; beyond it, pure knowledge, the Lord, and eternal Śiva, knowledge-and-action in essence, enter as special powers into the syllable au, shaped as assent, formed of unsurpassed power. Hence the supreme emission, shaped as creation above and below: the breath-out to be breathed. Of the heart-seed so formed — shaped as the great mantra, shaped as the world, beyond the world — supreme Śiva Himself, as the seat where all rising comes to rest, is its own nature: all-shapedness, then shapelessness, each in turn the cause. Whoever truly knows such a heart-seed, and enters it — he is initiated in the highest sense: this very knowing, with no sesame-and-ghee oblation, is initiation in truth. Still breathing, living as men live, he is free while living; and when the body falls, he becomes the Lord, supreme Śiva Himself.
